issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(a) of the Code of Civil Procedure when a meaningful reading shows that clever drafting creates only an illusory cause of action and the suit is vexatious or meritless.

A plaint may be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure when the suit is barred by limitation, and a plaintiff cannot avoid that bar through clever drafting or by omitting a necessary challenge to an earlier instrument.

When deciding an application to reject a plaint under Order VII Rule 11, the court must assess the plaint’s averments as a whole and cannot rely on the written statement or the defendant’s contentions.
